tracks.label: 2+ years
tracks.title: Build strong foundations
tracks.expect: Interviewers test whether you understand the language and can write working code. They ask how things work, then give you a small problem to solve.
tracks.advice: Write the code yourself instead of only reading the answer, and be ready to explain one project clearly.

focus.why: The first round at almost every company: data structures, decorators and the object model.
Most early-career roles include a coding test or live coding.
Know how a FastAPI request flows and how to structure a small service.
Expect pytest fixtures and mocking.
Useful if the role touches data: pandas and pipelines.
Be able to explain threads, async and the GIL.

tracks.label: 6+ years
tracks.title: Show production depth
tracks.expect: Interviewers assume you know the basics and ask why and what if. They want trade-offs and failures you've handled.
tracks.advice: For each topic, prepare one real story from your own work, with numbers.

focus.why: The questions move to internals and language trade-offs.
Expect the GIL, async and when each model fits.
Expect API design, dependencies and error handling.
Expect resilience, caching and production behaviour.
Delivery guarantees and consumers come up often.
Know your testing strategy, not only the syntax.
Many companies still give a coding round.
Increasingly asked: know RAG and tool calling at a high level.
Know how pipelines are orchestrated.

tracks.label: 12+ years
tracks.title: Lead with design and judgement
tracks.expect: Interviewers test your judgement: what you would build, and why. Expect design problems, trade-offs and incidents you've led.
tracks.advice: Practise out loud, and always state the trade-off and the numbers.

focus.why: The centre of the interview: system design, capacity and resilience.
Event-driven design: ordering, delivery guarantees and recovery.
Expect to justify a concurrency model with evidence.
Reference architecture, guardrails and cost.
API strategy and service structure.
Pipelines and orchestration decisions.
Short but sharp checks on the language.
Some companies still include a coding round.
Focus on testing strategy across teams.
